name: Rolf Landauer
summary: German-born physicist and IBM researcher known for Landauer's Principle.

name: Léon Brillouin
summary: French-American physicist and Landauer's Ph.D. supervisor at Harvard.

name: John von Neumann
summary: Hungarian-American mathematician who influenced the connection between logic and thermodynamics.

name: John Swanson
summary: Computer scientist and physicist, friend and colleague of Landauer at IBM.

name: Charles Bennett
summary: IBM researcher and co-worker who popularized Landauer's Principle.

name: IBM
summary: Technology corporation where Landauer worked from 1952.

name: Harvard University
summary: University where Landauer earned his Ph.D. and studied in the late 1940s.

name: IBM Research Laboratory in Poughkeepsie
summary: IBM facility in New York where Landauer joined in 1952.

name: Irreversibility and Heat Generation in the Computing Process
summary: Groundbreaking paper published by Landauer in the IBM journal in July 1961.

name: Science and Information Theory
summary: Book by Brillouin summarizing the Negentropy principle and information theory.

name: Physical versus Logical Coupling in Memory System
summary: Paper by Swanson applying information theory to magnetic memories.

name: The Thermodynamics of Computation
summary: Foundational paper by Bennett that popularized Landauer's Principle.
